selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 19 or 20, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 20 at about 12:14 ET, less the stories earlier pages already used, plus every transcript from the fixed transcript sources dated in that window (House and Senate floor speeches from the Congressional Record of Nov. 19 and White House statements). Transcripts from Nov. 13 to 18 were searched only to confirm quotes. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Quotes under five words were left out, as were one official's account of what another said and statements by officials outside the offices in scope. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them; entries beginning "Reported as" are the reporter's wording.
lede: Nov. 19 and 20 brought Senate passage of a bipartisan permitting bill, a Senate vote on ending the war in Iran, President Trump's three-way summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, and a House Homeland Security Committee hearing with Secretary Markwayne Mullin. On the House floor, members spoke on the federal debt and spending, the Epstein files and the record of the outgoing Congress; senators also spoke on rural health funding, the defense authorization bill, prediction markets and lithium-ion battery fires.

This page lists what officeholders in scope were quoted saying in that coverage and in the day's Congressional Record: 344 statements from 50 speakers. Most come from floor speeches, which are printed verbatim in the Record.

Statements that make a checkable factual claim, or rest on a stated factual premise, are checked one at a time against AskAmerica's warehouse and primary sources. Checks still queued are marked "not yet checked" and the page is updated as results return. Each checked statement's test, finding and sources are shown with it.
